big_idea: We measure LENGTH and TIME with the right TOOLS and UNITS.
learning_intention: We are learning to measure with the right tool.
student_learning_goal: I can measure length and time using the right tool.
success_criteria: I can pick non-standard or standard units.
I can use cm and m with benchmarks.
I can use a RULER starting at zero.
I can describe TIME in seconds/minutes/hours.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Roo: Today's MARATHON — 4 stations: pick a unit, use cm/m, ruler, time! Be the MEASURE MAVEN! Roo + Cal open: 'SMALL unit, BIG count — BIG unit, small count! Right TOOL, right NUMBER!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets in lab coats. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL: non-standard units, cm/m, ruler, time.'

Review: 'Pick UNIT. Use cm/m + benchmarks. Ruler from ZERO. Time in s/min/hour.'

Now show the 4 stations:
- Station 1: PICK UNIT — measure 3 objects with the right unit (cubes/hand-spans/footsteps).
- Station 2: cm/m — estimate 4 lengths using benchmarks.
- Station 3: RULER — measure 4 objects in cm. Draw a 7-cm line.
- Station 4: TIME — pick units for 4 events.

Each child rotates and records on TEMPLATE.

'Roo and Cal say — every Measure Maven picks the right TOOL and UNIT.'

Review key rules:
- 'Smaller unit, more units needed.'
- '100 cm = 1 m.'
- 'Ruler starts at ZERO.'
- '60 seconds = 1 minute. 60 minutes = 1 hour.'

'Welcome to the MEASURE MARATHON!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 4 stations rotation (~6 min each).

STRATEGY COMPARE at Station 3 (RULER): two children measure the same pencil — one starting at 0, one starting at 2. Class confirms both can be right with proper subtraction. Cite Stephan & Clements measurement-length progression.
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'Same pencil, two starts. Length = end MINUS start.'

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: picks unit; uses cm/m; uses ruler; picks time unit.

discussion_prompts: How many cm in a metre?
Where do we start on a ruler?
consolidation.exit_routine: Closing capstone refrain — Roo + Cal call: 'SMALL unit, BIG count!' Class: 'BIG unit, small count!' Cal: 'Right TOOL, right NUMBER!' (3x). Each child shares one station's attribute, tool, and reading.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child uses the WRONG TOOL — repairing the tool-mismatch trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the capstone (4 stations, each measuring a different attribute with the right tool), the trap is attribute-tool mismatch: child uses ruler for mass or stopwatch for length. Lehrer (2003) and Stephan & Clements measurement-length progressions place attribute-tool matching as the unit's terminal target — without it, the unit's content has not transferred.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: pick units (L1), standard cm/m (L2), ruler use (L3), time tools (L4) into a 4-attribute marathon.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone Station 4. Child tries to use a ruler to time 'how long brushing teeth takes'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Roo asks — does a RULER measure TIME? No, it measures LENGTH.'

Guide. 'For TIME, use a stopwatch or a clock. For LENGTH, use a ruler.'

Generlise. 'Pick TOOL by ATTRIBUTE: ruler for length, stopwatch for time, balance for mass, container for capacity.'
common_misconceptions: Any tool measures any thing. (Repair: tool matches attribute.)
All tools are the same. (Repair: rulers ≠ stopwatches.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child uses ruler for mass: 'Pause. What is MASS? What does mass FEEL like? What TOOL helps?' Child re-tools.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses right tool but reads wrong (e.g., starts ruler at 1): drill the Lesson 3 'count SPACES, start at 0' rule.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child measures correctly but can't articulate WHY this tool: force the sentence frame 'I picked the ___ because I'm measuring ___.'

parts_outline.task: Match 4 objects to the right unit (cubes/hand-spans/cm/m).
Measure 3 objects with a ruler. Draw a 6-cm line.
Pick time units for 4 everyday events.

expected_image_assets: Roo and Cal in worksheet header
